Thanks for the ping, Lauren. I pulled the signup logs and attached the CSV with the raw events (sequence numbers, session tokens). Quick observations:
- The signup completed 00:02 after email verification — unusually fast compared to typical signups (~2-10 min with manual steps).
- The IP (52.12.34.210) has been used for 8 signups in the last 30 minutes across different domains.
- The initial usage pattern: within 18 minutes they consumed ~1,800 tokens via automated burst calls (heavy short-completion usage).

I'll attach an IP lookup screenshot and a short dump of similar domains pointed at the same mail forwarder. Seems like either a bot farm or a single org using disposable forwarding to spin test accounts.

[Attachment: ip-lookup.png (PNG, 48KB)]
[Attachment: suspicious-domains.txt (TXT, 3KB)]

Recommend: hold the request for credit extension, and — unless Neha sees signals that contradict — we should revoke the extra credits and mark the account for manual verification if they escalate. Happy to jump on a call.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Trust & Safety Analyst, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 11:28:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Automated alert — possible abuse flagged on new credit issuance

Adding my assessment after triaging the evidence. Summary:
- Verdict: High likelihood of abuse (70-85% confidence).
- Key signals: disposable MX, domain aged ~2 weeks, same IP cluster, immediate high-rate token usage with identical prompt patterns across clusters.
- Recommendation: Revoke promotional credits (reverse grant) and lock the account pending verification. Escalate to legal if they request chargebacks.

If Sales wants to offer an alternative for a legitimate customer, suggest the following verification steps before manually re-granting credits:
1) Company website URL and LinkedIn org page that matches the requestor's name/email domain.
2) A company-owned email domain (not a forwarding or disposable mailbox).
3) Short call or calendar invite from an @metacraft.ai address or an enterprise SSO claim.

I'll also prepare a short rule tweak for the credit engine to add a 'disposable-mx + domain-age < 90 days' hard filter for auto-extensions. Dev, can you estimate effort?

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Hi Sam — thanks for trying Redwood and for your message. I wanted to follow up quickly with what our team found during a manual review of your account request.

We ran a quick internal check and observed a few signals that required verification before we can approve a promotional extension: the email route appears to be a forwarding/disposable provider, the domain metacraft.ai is recently registered, and there were multiple signups from the same IP block that match known bot patterns. Because of the risk, we have temporarily held the requested extension and rolled back the additional credits issued earlier.

If MetaCraft Labs is a legitimate company and you'd like us to reconsider, please reply with one of the following for verification: a company website URL + LinkedIn page, or a corporate email from a non-forwarding mail host. Once we confirm, I can manually grant a one-time extension. We appreciate your understanding — happy to expedite if you can provide the verification items.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
